With U.S. bond markets closed for Independence Day, Bitcoin is holding steady at $62,480 — a +1.29% gain over 24 hours — as markets digest Thursday's historic NFP miss (57K vs. 110K consensus). The DXY settled at 100.86 heading into the long weekend, and the 10-year Treasury last printed at 4.49%, both reflecting the market's repricing of September rate-hike probability sharply lower.

Institutional flows have turned structurally positive. Fidelity's FBTC led July 3 inflows with $166 million, contributing to $221.7 million in total daily net inflows — ending a 10-session outflow streak that had drained $2.7 billion. Separately, Revolut announced it will delist Tether's USDT by August 31 to comply with EU MiCA requirements, adding further stablecoin market structure pressure. A weakened dollar, retreating yields, and returning ETF demand are collectively providing the first synchronized tailwinds for digital assets since early Q1.
